chunks: My father and a group of my scholars narrated to me from Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah and Muhammad ibn Yahya and 'Abdillah ibn Ja'far Al-Himyari and Ahmad ibn Idris, all from Al-Husayn ibn 'Ubaydillah, from Al-Hasan ibn 'Ali ibn Abi 'Uthman, from 'Abd al-Jabbar Al-Nahawandi, from Abi Sa'id, from Al-Husayn ibn Thuwayr ibn Abi Fakhtah, who said:

Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: O Husayn! Whoever leaves his house intending to visit the grave of Husayn ibn 'Ali (peace be upon him), if he is walking, Allah will record for him one good deed for every step and erase one bad deed from him. Until when he arrives in the Hā'ir, Allah will record him among the successful and the chosen [the triumphant and the victorious]. Until when he completes his rituals, Allah will record him among the winners. Until when he intends to depart, an angel comes to him and says: Verily, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) sends you greetings and says to you: Resume your deeds, for what has passed of your sins has been forgiven.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual rewards for walking to visit the grave of Imam Husayn (a.s.)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat* highlights the cumulative spiritual merit of physically traveling to Imam Husayn’s shrine, where each step serves as an expiation for sins. It concludes with a unique divine interaction where the Prophet Muhammad (s.a.w.) greets the pilgrim and commands them to 'resume worship,' implying that the Ziyarah itself constitutes a complete act of devotion that resets one’s spiritual standing.
